items.title: Grad-CAM silently overwrites an existing user volume with a matching name

findings.title: Grad-CAM silently overwrites an existing user volume with a matching name
findings.evidence:
xaiNodeName = f"{displayReferenceNode.GetName()}_GradCAM"

                    xaiNode = slicer.mrmlScene.GetFirstNodeByName(xaiNodeName)
                    if not xaiNode or not xaiNode.IsA("vtkMRMLScalarVolumeNode"):
                        xaiNode = slicer.mrmlScene.AddNewNodeByClass("vtkMRMLScalarVolumeNode", xaiNodeName)

                    # Model heatmap is [X,Y,Z]; Slicer expects array order [K,J,I] = [Z,Y,X].
                    heatmap_kji = np.transpose(heatmap_xyz, (2, 1, 0))
                    slicer.util.updateVolumeFromArray(xaiNode, heatmap_kji)
findings.explanation: If an unrelated loaded scalar volume is already named like the input plus _GradCAM, requesting XAI replaces its image data without confirmation. Saving the scene or that volume afterward can make the unintended loss persistent.
findings.suggestion: Always create a uniquely named result node, or track only nodes created by this module and explicitly confirm replacement.

gpt.reason: GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py:746-750,754-755: `xaiNode = slicer.mrmlScene.GetFirstNodeByName(xaiNodeName)` and `slicer.util.updateVolumeFromArray(xaiNode, heatmap_kji)`. A same-named scalar volume is reused without ownership check or confirmation, replacing image data and orientation; saving it can persist the loss. This requires successful classification and XAI generation.

gemini.reason: In GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py lines 746-754, the code reuses an existing `vtkMRMLScalarVolumeNode` in the in-memory MRML scene if its name matches `<displayReferenceNode>_GradCAM`, and calls `slicer.util.updateVolumeFromArray(xaiNode, heatmap_kji)`. However, this only updates an in-memory MRML node named `*_GradCAM` (evidently intended to update a previous Grad-CAM heatmap on re-run rather than cluttering the scene) and does not overwrite any files on disk without user action. Under the review policy, this is a minor UI/node-management issue, not a blocking safety issue.

items.title: Missing `PreProcessing/model_manager.py` in `MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS` causes packaged builds to fail at runtime

findings.title: Missing `PreProcessing/model_manager.py` in `MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS` causes packaged builds to fail at runtime
findings.evidence:
set(MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS
  ${MODULE_NAME}.py

  PreProcessing/__init__.py
  PreProcessing/apply_classification.py
  PreProcessing/apply_n4.py
  PreProcessing/apply_norm.py
  PreProcessing/apply_skull.py
  PreProcessing/apply_XAI.py
  PreProcessing/densenet_model.py
  PreProcessing/prepare_classification.py
  PreProcessing/resnet_model.py

  )
findings.explanation: `GliomaClassifier.py` imports `from PreProcessing import model_manager` (line 636) when running classification, and `model_manager.ensure_model` is used to download and verify the ResNet10, ResNet50, and DenseNet121 models. However, `PreProcessing/model_manager.py` is omitted from `MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS` in `GliomaClassifier/CMakeLists.txt`, so it will not be installed in packaged builds and classification will fail with `ImportError: cannot import name 'model_manager' from 'PreProcessing'`.
findings.suggestion: Add `PreProcessing/model_manager.py` to `MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS` in `GliomaClassifier/CMakeLists.txt`.

gpt.reason: GliomaClassifier/CMakeLists.txt:5-18,26-30 lists PreProcessing scripts but not model_manager.py; GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py:636 unconditionally says `from PreProcessing import model_manager` during classification, before selecting models. Packaged classification fails, but the import is not at module load, so this is an ordinary runtime functionality failure rather than a broken catalog entry or module load.

gemini.reason: In GliomaClassifier/CMakeLists.txt lines 5-18, `PreProcessing/model_manager.py` is omitted from `MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS`, while `GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py` line 636 executes `from PreProcessing import model_manager` unconditionally during classification. In packaged builds, `slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule` only installs the listed scripts, so running classification fails with `ImportError`. Because this breaks the core functionality of packaged builds, it is a blocking packaging defect.

items.title: PyTorch is installed directly via `pip_install("torch")` instead of `PyTorchUtils`

findings.title: PyTorch is installed directly via `pip_install("torch")` instead of `PyTorchUtils`
findings.evidence:
except ModuleNotFoundError:
        logging.info("PyTorch not found. Installing...")
        slicer.util.pip_install("typing_extensions>=4.10.0")
        slicer.util.pip_install("torch")
        importlib.invalidate_caches()
findings.explanation: Instead of using the Slicer `PyTorch` extension (`PyTorchUtils`) to check and install PyTorch with hardware-appropriate wheels and user confirmation, `ensure_torch_installed()` directly calls `slicer.util.pip_install("torch")` from PyPI without user confirmation. Additionally, `nipreps-synthstrip` (`apply_skull.py` line 16) also declares `torch` as a pip dependency and can pull PyPI `torch` if PyTorch is not yet installed. Per the Slicer Extensions Index review policy, PyTorch must be installed exclusively via `PyTorchUtils` from the `PyTorch` extension.
findings.suggestion: Use `PyTorchUtils.PyTorchUtilsLogic()` from the Slicer `PyTorch` extension to check for and install PyTorch (and ensure PyTorch is installed via `PyTorchUtils` before installing `nipreps-synthstrip`). Add `"PyTorchUtils"` to `self.parent.dependencies` in `GliomaClassifier`.

findings.title: PyTorch is installed directly with pip instead of through the PyTorch extension
findings.evidence:
except ModuleNotFoundError:
        logging.info("PyTorch not found. Installing...")
        slicer.util.pip_install("typing_extensions>=4.10.0")
        slicer.util.pip_install("torch")
        importlib.invalidate_caches()
findings.explanation: When PyTorch is absent, selecting a PyTorch model causes an unconfirmed pip installation into the shared Slicer environment, bypassing the declared PyTorch extension's platform-specific installation handling. It can install an incompatible build or alter dependencies used by other extensions.
findings.suggestion: Use PyTorchUtils from the declared PyTorch extension and obtain user confirmation before any large download.

gpt.reason: GliomaClassifier/PreProcessing/apply_classification.py:40-44: `slicer.util.pip_install("torch")` follows a missing-PyTorch exception without a confirmation dialog; lines 196-198 call the helper for PyTorch inference. This bypasses the required PyTorch extension installation mechanism and changes the shared environment. The separately claimed SynthStrip transitive dependency could not be verified from repository metadata.

gemini.reason: In GliomaClassifier/PreProcessing/apply_classification.py lines 40-44, `ensure_torch_installed()` runs `slicer.util.pip_install("typing_extensions>=4.10.0")` and `slicer.util.pip_install("torch")` without user confirmation instead of using `PyTorchUtils` from the `PyTorch` extension. Similarly, `GliomaClassifier/PreProcessing/apply_skull.py` line 16 runs `slicer.util.pip_install("nipreps-synthstrip")` which depends on `torch`. The Slicer Extensions Index review policy explicitly requires requesting changes (blocking) when PyTorch is installed via `pip_install("torch")` rather than `PyTorchUtils`.

items.title: Unprompted installation of `tensorflow==2.13.0` downgrades bundled packages and conflicts with PyTorch dependencies

findings.explanation: When TensorFlow is not installed, `ensure_tensorflow_installed()` runs `slicer.util.pip_install("tensorflow==2.13.0")` without asking the user for confirmation before downloading hundreds of megabytes. Furthermore, `tensorflow==2.13.0` strictly pins `numpy<=1.24.3` and `typing-extensions<4.6.0`, which downgrades Slicer's bundled `numpy` and conflicts with PyTorch's requirement (`typing_extensions>=4.10.0` in the same file at line 42), breaking Slicer's shared Python environment and Note: `tensorflow==2.13.0` also has no wheels for Python 3.12 (used in Slicer 5.9+).
findings.suggestion: Prompt the user via `slicer.util.confirmOkCancelDisplay` before installing large packages like TensorFlow or SynthStrip, avoid hard-pinning old TensorFlow versions (`tensorflow==2.13.0`) that downgrade Slicer's bundled `numpy` or conflict with `typing_extensions`, and ensure compatibility with Slicer's Python version.

items.title: All three volume selectors in the UI bind to the same `inputVolume` parameter node property

findings.title: All three volume selectors in the UI bind to the same `inputVolume` parameter node property
findings.evidence:
<property name="SlicerParameterName" stdset="0">
               <string>inputVolume</string>
              </property>
findings.explanation: In `GliomaClassifier.ui`, three distinct `qMRMLNodeComboBox` widgets (`inputSelector` on line 78, `inputSelector_1` on line 308, and `inputSelector_2` on line 349) all have `SlicerParameterName` set to `inputVolume`. When `self._parameterNode.connectGui(self.ui)` runs, all three selectors bind to the same `inputVolume` property on the parameter node, causing selecting a T1-CE volume (`inputSelector_1`) and a FLAIR volume (`inputSelector_2`) to overwrite each other.
findings.suggestion: Define separate fields on `GliomaClassifierParameterNode` (e.g., `inputVolume`, `t1cVolume`, `flairVolume`) or remove the duplicate `SlicerParameterName` dynamic properties from `inputSelector_1` and `inputSelector_2`.

gpt.reason: GliomaClassifier/Resources/UI/GliomaClassifier.ui:77-79,307-309,348-350 each contain `<string>inputVolume</string>`; GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py:306-308 calls `self._parameterNode.connectGui(self.ui)`, and lines 608-609 read both selectors. Duplicate binding is verified, but Slicer's connectGui implementation is not in this repository and its handling of duplicate parameter names was not inspected, so whether both selectors synchronize or only one is connected cannot be established here.

gemini.reason: In GliomaClassifier/Resources/UI/GliomaClassifier.ui, `inputSelector` (lines 77-79), `inputSelector_1` (lines 307-309), and `inputSelector_2` (lines 348-350) all set `SlicerParameterName` to `inputVolume`. When `self._parameterNode.connectGui(self.ui)` runs in `GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py` line 308, all three `qMRMLNodeComboBox` selectors bind to `self._parameterNode.inputVolume`, causing selection changes in one selector to overwrite the others. This is a major soundness bug.

items.title: Installed model directory does not match the runtime model paths

findings.title: Installed model directory does not match the runtime model paths
findings.evidence:
# Install model files
install(
  DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/Resources/Models
  DESTINATION ${Slicer_INSTALL_QTSCRIPTEDMODULES_LIB_DIR}/${MODULE_NAME}/Resources
)
findings.explanation: GliomaClassifierLogic constructs its model paths relative to the directory containing GliomaClassifier.py, under Resources/Models (GliomaClassifier.py:947-965), but this rule installs them under an additional GliomaClassifier/Resources directory. Thus the installed default classifier and skull stripping cannot find their bundled models at their expected paths; optional models are also cached under the script directory, which may not be writable.
findings.suggestion: Install bundled models where the module resolves them, or consistently resolve the actual install location, and use a writable user cache for optional downloads.

gpt.reason: GliomaClassifier/CMakeLists.txt:35-37 installs `DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/Resources/Models` to `${Slicer_INSTALL_QTSCRIPTEDMODULES_LIB_DIR}/${MODULE_NAME}/Resources`, whereas GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py:947-954 and 960-965 use `moduleDir`, `"Resources"`, `"Models"`. The extra module-name directory mismatches the script-relative paths in a standard scripted-module layout. Moreover the inspected Resources listing contains no Models directory, so the install rule may fail before runtime; a build and writable installation were not tested.

gemini.reason: In GliomaClassifier/CMakeLists.txt lines 35-38, `install(DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/Resources/Models DESTINATION ${Slicer_INSTALL_QTSCRIPTEDMODULES_LIB_DIR}/${MODULE_NAME}/Resources)` installs models into `<lib>/GliomaClassifier/Resources/Models`, whereas `slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule` installs `GliomaClassifier.py` into `<lib>/` and `GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py` lines 947-986 looks for models at `os.path.join(moduleDir, "Resources", "Models", ...)`. Moreover, `Resources/Models` does not even exist in the repository at commit 3ff5b4b649f4 (as verified with `list_files` on `GliomaClassifier/Resources`), so CMake configuration/installation will fail on the missing directory and bundled models (`synthstrip.1.pt`, `proposed_model_final.h5`) are absent. This is a blocking packaging defect.

findings.title: `UnboundLocalError` for `suffix` in `process()` when `applyRAS` is False
findings.explanation: In `GliomaClassifierLogic.process()`, `suffix` is only initialized if `applyRAS` is `True`. If the user runs preprocessing with `applyRAS` unchecked (for example, selecting only Skull Stripping, N4, or Normalization, or none of them), accessing `suffix` raises `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'suffix' where it is not associated with a value`.
findings.suggestion: Initialize `suffix = ""` before `if applyRAS:`.

findings.title: Preprocessing requires RAS to be selected because suffix is uninitialized
findings.explanation: If RAS orientation is unchecked, selecting skull stripping, N4 or normalization attempts to append to an uninitialized local variable. With no operations selected, outputName also uses that undefined variable. The UI otherwise permits these combinations, so normal preprocessing fails.
findings.suggestion: Initialize suffix to an empty string before checking any options and test each operation independently.

gpt.reason: GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py:1020-1024: `if applyRAS:` is the only initialization of `suffix`, followed by `suffix += "_Strip"`; lines 1026-1032 similarly use it for N4, normalization and the output name. The UI supplies independently selectable checkboxes (Resources/UI/GliomaClassifier.ui:161-190), so preprocessing without RAS fails with UnboundLocalError.

gemini.reason: In GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py lines 1020-1032, `suffix` is only assigned (`suffix = "_RAS"`) inside `if applyRAS:`. If `applyRAS` is `False`, any subsequent `suffix += ...` or `outputName = inputVolume.GetName() + suffix` raises `UnboundLocalError` because `suffix` was never initialized to `""`. This is a major soundness bug.

findings.title: `UnboundLocalError` for `suffix` in `process()` when `applyRAS` is False
findings.explanation: In `GliomaClassifierLogic.process()`, `suffix` is only initialized if `applyRAS` is `True`. If the user runs preprocessing with `applyRAS` unchecked (for example, selecting only Skull Stripping, N4, or Normalization, or none of them), accessing `suffix` raises `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'suffix' where it is not associated with a value`.
findings.suggestion: Initialize `suffix = ""` before `if applyRAS:`.

findings.title: Preprocessing requires RAS to be selected because suffix is uninitialized
findings.explanation: If RAS orientation is unchecked, selecting skull stripping, N4 or normalization attempts to append to an uninitialized local variable. With no operations selected, outputName also uses that undefined variable. The UI otherwise permits these combinations, so normal preprocessing fails.
findings.suggestion: Initialize suffix to an empty string before checking any options and test each operation independently.

gpt.reason: GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py:1020-1024: `if applyRAS:` is the only initialization of `suffix`, followed by `suffix += "_Strip"`; lines 1026-1032 similarly use it for N4, normalization and the output name. The UI supplies independently selectable checkboxes (Resources/UI/GliomaClassifier.ui:161-190), so preprocessing without RAS fails with UnboundLocalError.

gemini.reason: In GliomaClassifier/GliomaClassifier.py lines 1020-1032, `suffix` is only assigned (`suffix = "_RAS"`) inside `if applyRAS:`. If `applyRAS` is `False`, any subsequent `suffix += ...` or `outputName = inputVolume.GetName() + suffix` raises `UnboundLocalError` because `suffix` was never initialized to `""`. This is a major soundness bug.
